correctness.rationale: Both graphs are explicitly defined by fifteen edges and the all-rest hitting time is exact for every one of 59049 labelled base-three configurations. Three different complete enumerators (vectorized Python, imperative C++17, and independently constructed graph geometries in Python) agree on all five time bins and all terminal-wave coefficients; all states satisfy F^4(x)=0. The short-cycle lemma is proven by intersecting two two-element subsets of three excited sites. No sampling or infinite extrapolation is used. Risks are programming errors shared across interpretations, reduced by independent graph constructions; full numerical counts are exact finite computations, not a general arbitrary-graph bound.

value.rationale: The two unique ten-vertex generalized Petersen cubic geometries are a natural complete pair, and the same documented one-contact dynamics supports qualitatively different long periods on them. Increasing the contact threshold to two destroys all oscillations within exactly four steps on both, while the exact late-wave population differs 3380 versus 1520, and the initial excitation support threshold differs 3 versus 4. The latter difference is explained by a universal four-cycle obstruction, giving a structural reason tied to girth instead of an arbitrary numerical slice. Exact first-rest and seed-weight distributions are natural response-time invariants useful for comparing propagation/quenched activity under threshold changes. The inference is limited to this pair; no general cubic-graph law is claimed.
